text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- An interior ministry report to be published today shows that local authorities have saved 27 percent on annual budgets by putting out to tender public services. At the same time putting out to tender has not harmed either service or quality, the report states.

--- The Russian government wants Danish authorities to drop a fine of more than four million crowns which the Copenhagen police demand from airline company Aeroflot for flying 617 foreigners without visas to Copenhagen over the course of several years.

--- Local authorities are receiving reports from locals on foreigners -- mainly Germans -- who buy houses zoned for permanent residential use and use them illegally for holidays only. Four German houseowners have been ordered by the police to sell their houses in Denmark within the next six months.
--- 70 percent of Danish adults want to keep film censorship, a new survey shows, supporting new culture minister Ebbe Lundgaard, who wants to retain film censorship, in contrast to his predecessor.

--- Denmark's largest bank Den Danske Bank has been left behind in the fight to gain PC banking customers by second largest bank Unibank which has built up Denmark's largest PC banking service in record time.

--- Workers and bosses agree on the need to reduce the welfare burden of the growing number of pensioners. The metalworkers' union wants workers over 60 years old to switch to part-time working rather than retire, while employers want to raise the retirement age to 63 from 60.
